speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, episodes of painful urination, and a history of a painful left ankle that resolved on its own. To begin my evaluation, are you currently experiencing any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The patient is a 17-year-old male with a classic presentation of the triad: urethritis (painful urination), arthritis (sequential involvement of the left ankle and now right knee), and a history of inconsistent condom use with multiple female partners, suggesting a likely preceding Chlamydia infection. The maternal history of rheumatoid arthritis is likely incidental given the acute onset and specific pattern of joint involvement.
